name: Hepatic Lobular Architecture, Couinaud Segments and Portal Hypertension

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Blumgart Surgery of the Liver
clinicalPearls: Couinaud classification divides liver into 8 independent functional segments, each with individual portal pedicle
Portal triad contains hepatic arteriole, portal venule, and bile ductule within Glisson capsule
Hepatic stellate (Ito) cells in space of Disse store vitamin A and transform into collagen-secreting myofibroblasts in fibrosis
Normal portal venous pressure is 5-10 mmHg; portal hypertension is defined by hepatic venous pressure gradient > 5 mmHg
Portosystemic anastomoses dilate in portal hypertension: esophageal varices, caput medusae, and hemorrhoids
reference.pathophysiology: The liver architecture organizes hepatocytes around microvascular sinusoids receiving dual blood supply from portal vein (75%) and hepatic artery (25%). Cirrhosis disrupts sinusoidal fenestrations and increases intrahepatic vascular resistance through stellate cell activation and fibrous scar deposition, driving blood backward into portosystemic collateral vessels.
additionalInvestigations: Abdominal Doppler ultrasound to assess portal vein flow and flow direction
Upper endoscopy (EGD) for screening and grading of esophageal varices
